note: Every sentence on the site that states a fact about Foundry's results, behaviour or decisions is one of these claims. app/site/test/claims.test.mjs checks that each source file exists under research/ and that every number in a claim's text appears in that file. Status words: Works now, Preview, Planned, Not decided, Decided, Limit. Evidence words: development (our own tests, not sealed), design, decided, documentation, literature.

C01.text: Nothing runs, sends or changes until you say yes. The limit: a coding agent that can run commands as you on this computer could do what you can do, including say yes.
C01.short: Nothing happens until you say yes (with one honest limit)

C02.text: In our tests, 10 of 10 attempts to get around your yes were refused.
C02.short: Ways around your yes are refused

C03.text: Tests use pretend data and pretend inboxes. Nothing real is sent during a test.

C04.text: In our own tests, a low-cost AI that practised first built a 14-case order process with 14 of 14 right, for $0.39. A top AI that built it in one go got 5 of 14, for $7.63.
C04.qualifier: Development tests on one task family we wrote, not a promise about yours.

C05.text: On 60 public development tasks, a low-cost AI with Foundry's procedure passed 18 of 60 for $0.94; a stronger AI alone passed 20 of 60 for $6.03.
C05.short: A low-cost AI with a procedure, at about a sixth of the cost
C05.qualifier: One run each on development tasks; the frozen test run has not been done.

C06.text: Of 10 sample n8n files, 2 came over exactly, 10 of 10 can be called as they are, and 0 were run.
C06.short: n8n import: honest about what comes over
C06.qualifier: A small, skewed sample of open-licence files; nothing was executed.

C07.text: In a simulated company, builds that passed their process check still applied 57 of 57 large refunds without approval. With the rule layer, 0 did, and a scripted auditor could answer its questions from the records.
C07.short: Rules that hold at run time (test bed only)
C07.qualifier: A test bed we built; this rule layer is not in the product yet.

C08.text: Free while one person decides, at any size, with single sign-on included. Paid only when a second person's yes or a rule owner has to count.

C09.text: Foundry runs only on this computer. Nothing is published or hosted.

C10.text: Bringing your own AI key is free, and the key goes into your computer's keychain, never into files or logs.

C11.text: People approve almost every single prompt (97% in one vendor's data) but reject whole plans far more often (39% versus 3%).
C11.short: Why Foundry asks once, about the whole plan
C11.qualifier: Vendor-published numbers, not a controlled study of Foundry.

C12.text: The earlier prototype went from request to first live run in 3 person actions.
C12.short: Three actions in the earlier prototype

C13.text: Tested on Linux only. macOS and Windows are untested, and steps that run code are refused there.

C14.text: Your decisions and the AI's transcripts are not yet part of the chained record, and its latest link is not stored outside this computer unless you ask for it.
